violations.text: The quaternary ammonium concentration in the sanitizing solution of the 3-bay sink was 0 parts per million (ppm) (chemical sanitizer observed not being siphoned through the tubing when wall unit turned on). According to the manufacturer's use directions, the concentration of the quaternary ammonium must be 200-400 ppm. Bleach sanitizer was properly setup in the sanitizer bay at 50-100 ppm for proper sanitizing at the time of inspection. Bleach to be properly tested and used for sanitizing until wall unit is adjusted/repaired. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/20/2026

Several items prepared on site were observed not marked with the date of preparation. Ready-to-eat time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods prepared in the establishment and held for more than 24 hours must be marked with the date of preparation. Per the PIC, all items were made within the week of inspection. PIC to date mark items to ensure they are not held longer than 7 days from the date of inspection unless frozen. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 08/20/2026

Pasta w/ Chicken was observed cooling in refrigeration in covered pans at 72 degrees Fahrenheit. Based on temperature and time of preparation, pans were uncovered to allow for rapid cooling at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 05/20/2025

At the time of inspection, a large, covered plastic container of tomato sauce that was prepped/cooked previous day was observed at 52 degrees Fahrenheit in refrigeration. The tomato sauce was not cooled properly to 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below within the total of 6 hours from previous day. Tomato Sauce was voluntarily disposed of at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 05/06/2025

At the time of inspection, several food items were observed cooling for later service in covered tin containers stacked on top of each other. Food items are to be arranged in the EQUIPMENT to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls, and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination. (Food items were separated and uncovered for rapid cooling at the time of inspection.) Proper cooling strategies were discussed with PIC. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 05/06/2025

Bowls are being used as scoops in containers of dry ingredients. Utensils used to dispense non-time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods such as sugar and flour must be stored in the food item with their handles above the top of the food within the container. Bowls were removed at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 05/06/2025
